cases.description: The byte order mark at byte 0 is skipped and the second U+FEFF is an ordinary character, so the line is a paragraph, not a heading (§5.1).

A U+FEFF after the byte order mark does not restart front matter detection, so the --- lines are Markdown: the first two lines form a setext heading of two lines, whose $title joins them with \n (§5.1, §5.3).
A U+FEFF inside a heading is Default_Ignorable, so step 2 of the slug rule removes it, and the derived anchor is foo (§5.1, §6.3).
A %YAML line in front matter is a syntax error, even for version 1.2, since the --- marker a directive needs would close the front matter (§4.4, decision I1.10).
A %YAML 1.1 line in front matter is also a syntax error, not yaml-version-unsupported (§4.4, decision I1.10).
